title: INT8 Calibration Coordinator and Runtime Hotpatch Strategy for KV-cache-heavy Models
creator: Marco Li
description:
Background: We observed quantization regressions for long-context LLMs when applying standard per-channel INT8 calibration combined with activation-scaling heuristics. Root cause investigation indicates that KV-cache-heavy inference traffic changes activation distributions across early vs late positions and exposes kernel numeric instability in fused attention kernels under small-scale rescale factors. Goal: Build an orchestration layer — the Calibration Coordinator — that stitches together: 1) per-workload calibration jobs (multi-dataset profiles), 2) channel-aware rescale candidate generation (including SmoothQuant-like ops but with per-layer stability scoring), 3) a runtime hotpatch strategy to deploy safe kernel fallbacks (FP16/FP8-friendly kernels or de-fused attention) dynamically when rollout telemetry shows divergence.

Scope and deliverables:
- Calibration Coordinator service (lightweight orchestrator): accepts workload descriptors, runs batched calibration trials with multiple sample sets (prefix-heavy, suffix-heavy, mixed), and produces a ranked list of quantization profiles (per-layer scale + bias suggestions) with stability scores and expected token error bounds.
- Golden prompt set: curated prompt sets that exercise KV-cache behaviour across sequence positions for validation/eval.
- Runtime hotpatch controller: ability to flip kernel implementations per-model-version at runtime (canary across 0.1/1/10% traffic), and automatic fallback rules triggered by metric thresholds (per-route token-level perplexity drift, token error delta, or increased generation instability).
- CI calibration harness integration: reusable pipeline that runs candidate profiles against the golden set and records metrics (LLR, PPL, semantic drift) into the eval dashboard.
- Rollout playbook and safety gates: indicators for canary promotion, automatic rollback criteria, and mitigations (throttled rollback, graceful concurrency drain).

Acceptance criteria:
- Coordinator can produce at least 3 ranked INT8 profiles for a given workload within target run-time (2x baseline calibration time) and exposes stability_score for each profile.
- When promoted to a 1% canary of production traffic for three representative models, the promoted INT8 profile must show no >1.5% drop in semantic similarity (embedding cosine on golden set) and no >2% increase in latency tail (p99).
- Hotpatch controller can switch kernel implementation for a live model without dropping active connections and completes the switch within 15s for a single server node.
- CI harness produces a daily report with regression alerts and stores calibration artifacts (profiles, histograms, perf traces) in our artifact bucket.

Technical notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer measuring profile stability with a hybrid score that combines activation distribution overlap (KL-divergence on collected histograms) and quantization sensitivity (change in logits / top-k token probability on the golden set). This allows us to rank profiles by expected semantic degradation rather than raw MSE.
- Kernel fallback options: (A) de-fused attention kernel in FP16, (B) alternative INT8 kernel with conservative rescale, (C) FP8 mixed kernel for layers passing activation safety. Fallback increases CPU/GPU cycles but reduces customer-visible regressions; coordinator must weigh cost delta.
- KV-cache specific testing: inject synthetic long-prefix traffic to emulate streaming applications; capture per-step activation drift and include in the stability_score computation.
- We will reuse parts of the existing calibration harness (ENG-27105 artifacts) but must avoid deterministic coupling to older per-layer heuristics—the coordinator will treat legacy heuristics as one candidate among many.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1-2: Prototype coordinator API and sample job runner (local). Deliverable: prototype that runs three calibration variants and outputs ranked JSON artifact.
- Week 3-4: Integrate golden-set CI evaluations and record metrics into eval dashboard. Deliverable: pipeline job and dashboard panels.
- Week 5: Implement runtime hotpatch controller proof-of-concept to change kernel variants for a single model on a dedicated node. Deliverable: hotpatch CLI and minimal controller.
- Week 6: Canary rollout automation + safety gates and alerting. Deliverable: canary orchestration workflow and runbook.
- Week 7: Performance tuning and documentation, handoff to SRE and release notes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Calibration runs may be expensive if we sample many sequences; mitigation: use stratified sampling with early-stopping when stability_score converges.
- Risk: Rollouts could degrade production quality; mitigation: conservative default to FP16 fallback, tight thresholds, and human-in-the-loop approvals for P0 customers.
- Risk: Kernel switch path may expose race conditions in KV-cache; mitigation: staged rollout on idle capacity and integration tests that validate cache consistency.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://drive.company.internal/drive/quant-coordinator-design (internal)
- Golden prompt set: gs://redwood-artifacts/quant/golden_sets/kv_cache_v1.jsonl

Notes for reviewers: Focus review on the stability_score definition (we need consensus on weights between KL and semantic drift) and on the kernel fallback API (atomicity guarantees).
